title: Normal projective birational models by Chow modification and normalization
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $S$ a nonempty integral proper finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist an integral finite-type $e$-scheme $Y$, a proper surjective $e$-morphism $c:Y\to S$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], a nonempty open $V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $c^{-1}V\to V$ an isomorphism, and a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_e$ over $e$ for some finite $n$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. For $n_Y:N=Y^\nu\to Y$, the normalization in its own function field [def-sc-normalization, def-sc-function-field], $n_Y$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], surjective and birational. The scheme $N$ is nonempty integral and normal: every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There exists a closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_e$ over $e$ for a finite $m$, so $Y$ and $N$ are H-projective [def-kun-projective], proper and finite type over $e$. The composite $c\circ n_Y:N\to S$ is proper, surjective and birational. The morphisms $c$, $n_Y$ and $c\circ n_Y$ induce isomorphisms on function fields. Birational means an isomorphism on suitable dense open subschemes; all function-field isomorphisms are those induced by the displayed morphisms.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150: finite normalization, with a birational Chow model inserted for projectivity. Stacks coherent.tex Tags 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), 0201 (remark-chow-Noetherian); varieties.tex Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic); finite-over-projective over the affine field base.

proof.text: Give the one-element group the identity actions on $e$ and $S$. These actions are compatible, and no faithfulness is needed. Apply [lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification] with $k=e$, $X=S$ and this group. Discard the actions. It gives an integral finite-type $e$-scheme $Y$, a proper surjective $e$-morphism $c:Y\to S$, an isomorphism $c^{-1}V\simeq V$ over a dense open $V\subseteq S$, and a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_e$ for a finite $n$. Since $S$ is nonempty and $V$ is dense open, $V$ is nonempty. Thus $c^{-1}V$ is nonempty as well.

source.place: Tag 0200, lemma-chow-Noetherian, and Tag 0201, remark-chow-Noetherian; trivial-group specialization of the existing equivariant Chow lemma.

proof.text: The scheme $Y$ is proper over $e$: its structure morphism is $Y\xrightarrow c S\to\operatorname{Spec}e$, a composite of proper morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; its spectrum is therefore Noetherian. As $Y$ is finite type over $e$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. Put $K=k(Y)$ and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be its generic-point morphism. The source has one point, is affine, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and integral; its only local ring is the field $K$, hence integrally closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), $a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tags 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); properties.tex Tag 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated); generic-point setup for Tags 035I and 035L.

proof.text: Form $n_Y:N=Y^\nu\to Y$ as in [def-sc-normalization]. This is the relative normalization of $Y$ in $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$: on each nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Y$, its preimage in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the whole point and has section ring $K$, so both constructions take the integral closure of $\mathcal O_Y(U)$ in $K$. Their affine gluing maps are the same restrictions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iv) to $a$ to conclude $N$ is integral, hence nonempty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks] to the same $a$ (the qcqs and normal-integral source hypotheses were checked in step 2) to conclude every local ring of $N$ is an integrally closed domain. Finally [lem-sc-normalization-exists], applied to the integral finite-type $e$-scheme $Y$, makes $n_Y$ finite, surjective and birational and makes $N$ proper over $e$, since $Y$ is proper.

To exhibit the normalization isomorphism open explicitly, choose a nonempty affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$. By [def-sc-normalization] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $n_Y^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B\subseteq K$ is the integral closure of $R$ and is finite as an $R$-module. Choose module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$; include $1$ if necessary. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], write $b_i=r_i/s_i$ in $K$, with $s_i\ne0$. For $s=\prod_i s_i\ne0$, the inclusions $R\subseteq B\subseteq K$ give $B[1/s]=R[1/s]$: all generators lie in $R[1/s]$, and the reverse inclusion comes from $R\subseteq B$. Thus $n_Y^{-1}D_U(s)\to D_U(s)$ is an isomorphism. This target open contains the generic point, and its nonempty inverse image is open in the integral $N$, so both opens are dense.

source.place: Tag 0BXC, lemma-normalization-birational; affine finite-module denominator argument (spelled out), and Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions.

proof.text: The embedding of $Y$ in step 1, together with its properness (so quasi-compactness), gives projectivity in [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] with base $\operatorname{Spec}e$, $T=Y$, and $h=n_Y$. This base is affine Noetherian, as checked in step 2. Its affine-base conclusion supplies a closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_e$ with finite $m$. These two embeddings are exactly H-projectivity in [def-kun-projective]. Both schemes are proper over $e$ by steps 2 and 3. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], proper includes finite type, giving the remaining finite-type assertion for $N$.

source.place: Tag 0GK4, lemma-normalize-projective; affine-base H-projective form supplied by lem-fin-finite-over-projective.

proof.text: The composite $b=c\circ n_Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. It is surjective: for $s\in S$, first lift $s$ to $y\in Y$ along $c$, then lift $y$ to $x\in N$ along $n_Y$. To check birationality explicitly, choose dense opens $A\subseteq N$ and $B\subseteq Y$ on which $n_Y$ is an isomorphism, as explicitly constructed in step 4. The open $D=B\cap c^{-1}V$ is nonempty because $Y$ is irreducible and both factors are nonempty opens. Under $c^{-1}V\simeq V$, its image is a nonempty open $W\subseteq V\subseteq S$, hence dense in the integral $S$. The open $A\cap n_Y^{-1}D$ is nonempty and therefore dense in integral $N$, and $b$ restricts there to the composite isomorphism $A\cap n_Y^{-1}D\simeq D\simeq W$. This proves birationality in the required dense-open sense.

source.place: Tags 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper) and 01RO (definition-birational); elementary intersection of the two already constructed isomorphism opens.

proof.text: For any of $c$, $n_Y$ and $b$, the preceding steps exhibit an isomorphism between nonempty opens of its integral source and target. Every such open contains the generic point, and the generic stalk is the function field [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction, def-sc-function-field]. An open restriction leaves that stalk unchanged (the neighborhoods inside an open neighborhood are cofinal). Hence taking the stalk map of each displayed open isomorphism gives an isomorphism of function fields, and this is the stalk map of the original morphism, since restriction uses the same sheaf maps. Stalk maps compose, so $b^*=n_Y^*\circ c^*$ under these identifications. Thus the asserted isomorphisms are all induced by the displayed morphisms.

source.place: Tags 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions) and 01RW (definition-function-field); generic-stalk restriction and composition.
